article: Central Limit Theorem: Conditions and Normal Approximation of the Sample Mean
scope: Compared the full Japanese source and twelve translations, definitions and assumptions, every displayed formula, proof sketch, history notes, Python simulation, Mermaid visualization, localized cross-links, metadata, and cited MIT course notes.
findings: Changed the main standardized statistic and sample-mean notation to Z_n and X-bar_n, making the sequence indexed by sample size explicit.
Replaced a diagram that conflated individual samples and sample means with one that shows repeated samples of size n, their means, and the distribution across many means.
Updated lastmod to 2026-11-24 across all thirteen language files; retained the original 2026-09-14 publication date.

meaning.note: Compared the complete text in all twelve languages; clarified repeated samples and the distribution of sample means, and made the indexed sequence explicit.

terminology.note: Checked CLT, i.i.d., sample mean, standard error, convergence in distribution, characteristic function, and related localized terms.

mathematics.note: Verified the finite-mean finite-positive-variance i.i.d. conditions, standardization, standard error identities, characteristic-function expansion and limit, and Cauchy example against MIT course notes.

code.note: Compared Python and Mermaid blocks across languages; Python simulation is unchanged and the diagram now shows repeated samples of size n and their sampling distribution.
